 Senior Citizen Age Above 60 Years: Must Check These 3 Important Things in November 2026
 Mitali 
 Mitali 
 Author 
 Follow 
 View profile 
 Last updated: 04 November 2026 
 Save

 Join Us 
 Follow Us 
 Add as Source 
 Senior Citizen Age Above 60 and a pensioner who depend on regular income from savings accounts, fixed deposits, recurring deposits and pension must check these three important things in November 2026.
 Table Of Content
 Pensioners Must Submit Their Annual Life Certificate 
 KYC and Government Facility 
 Update Nominee Details 
 1. Pensioners Must Submit Their Annual Life Certificate
 Senior Citizen above 60 years including senior citizens aged over 80 years should submit a life certificate by 30 November. 
 A life certificate or jeevan pramaan patra is a document which is furnished in physical form or Digital Life Certificate (DLC) generated through the Jeevan Pramaan platform using Aadhaar-based authentication.
 Submitting life certificate confirms that the pensioner is alive and eligible to continue receiving pension payments.
 Category 
 Last Date To Submit 
 Certificate Valid Till 
 Pensioners above 80 years 
 30 November 2026 
 One year from date of submission 
 All other government pensioners 
 30 November 2026

 Any time during the year

 Explore in Details - Life Certificate for Pensioners 2026: Eligibility, Benefits and Check Who Can Submit? 
 2. KYC and Government Facility
 Know Your Customer (KYC) is the process through which banks verify a customer's identity and address. 
 If your KYC is incomplete or overdue, bank may stop transactions or incoming payments, and recommends completing periodic updates when due. 
 How Often Should You Update Your KYC?
 Every bank account holder does not have to complete KYC every year. KYC updates depends generally on the customer's risk classification:
 Customer Risk Category 
 KYC Frequency 
 High-Risk 
 At least once every 2 years 
 Medium-Risk 
 At least once every 8 years 
 Low-Risk 
 At least once every 10 years 
 Senior citizens may find it difficult to visit a bank branch frequently. They may complete KYC from home through:
 Video Based Service 
 Doorstep Banking (you must check whether the bank offers facilities)
 Check Aadhaar and DBT Linkage for Government Benefits
 If you receive any government payments such as pension, scholarship, subsidy or other Benefit, then you must link Aadhaar to the bank account and the account should be linked for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) through the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) payment system, so government funds can be routed to the account.
 3. Update Nominee Details
 Many people open savings accounts, fixed deposits and recurring deposits but do not update nominee. If you do not add nominee details, it can create additional difficulties for family members when they need to claim the money after the account holder's death.
 Therefore, every account holder should check whether a nominee has been registered and whether the nominee's details are correct.
 Multiple Nominee Options
 Now you can may nominate up to four persons, either simultaneously or successively, thereby simplifying claim settlement for depositors and their nominees. under Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 .
 Simultaneous Nomination
 Depositors can divide their deposit amount among up to four nominees by specifying each person's share. The total share must equal 100%.
 For Example - For ₹10 Lakh Bank FD.
 Nominee 
 Share 
 Amount (₹) 
 Mother 
 40% 
 400000 
 Son 
 30% 
 300000 
 Daughter 
 20% 
 200000 
 Sister 
 10% 
 100000 
 Total 
 100% 
 1000000 
 Successive Nomination
 Account holder can name up to four nominees in order. If the first nominee dies, the second nominee becomes eligible, followed by the next nominees in the specified order.
 Here, successive nomination is not the same as dividing the deposit into four percentage shares. It establishes an order of priority.
 What Happens If There Is No Nominee?
 If a bank account holder dies without registering a nominee, family members may need to complete additional formalities to claim the money.
 Depending on the bank's rules and the circumstances, the bank may ask for additional documents such as:
 Death certificate of the account holder
 Identity proof of the claimant
 Claim application and declarations
 Legal heir certificate or succession certificate, wherever required
 Indemnity bond or declaration
 Other supporting documents requested by the bank
 Therefore, registering a nominee and keeping the information updated can help reduce difficulties for family members.
